en: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, from Qatadah, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: A man said to Ibn 'Umar: How did you hear the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) speaking about the private confidential discourse (al-najwa)? He said: I heard him saying: "The believer will be brought near to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection until He places His veil over him and makes him confess his sins, saying: 'Do you recognize [this]?' He will say: 'O my Lord, I recognize [it].' He will say: 'Indeed, I concealed them for you in the world, and indeed I forgive them for you today.' Then he will be given the record of his good deeds. As for the disbelievers and the hypocrites, they will be called out before the heads of all creation: 'These are the ones who lied against Allah.'"

Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abbad ibn Jabalah ibn Abi Rawwad narrated to us: Harami ibn 'Umarah narrated to us: Shaddad Abu Talhah al-Rasibi narrated to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, from Abu Burdah, from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "On the Day of Resurrection, people from among the Muslims will come with sins like mountains, and Allah will forgive them for them and place them upon the Jews and the Christians"—as far as I think. Abu Rawh said: I do not know from whom the doubt was. Abu Burdah said: So I narrated it to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, and he said: "Did your father narrate this to you from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" I said: "Yes."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna both narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith: Hammam informed us: Qatadah narrated to us with this chain of transmission similar to the hadith of 'Affan, and he said: "'Awn ibn 'Utbah."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us that 'Awn and Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah narrated to him that they both witnessed Abu Burdah narrating to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "No Muslim man dies except that Allah admits in his place a Jew or a Christian into the Fire." He said: So 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz adjured him by Allah, besides Whom there is no deity, three times that his father narrated it to him from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he swore to him. He said: And Sa'id did not narrate to me that he adjured him, nor did he contest 'Awn's statement.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Yahya, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will hand over to every Muslim a Jew or a Christian, and He will say: 'This is your ransom from the Fire.'"

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, with this chain of transmission similar to the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh, and he added to it: "So Allah inspired to this [land]: 'Become distant,' and to that [land]: 'Draw near.'"

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to me: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, that he heard Aba al-Siddiq al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "A man killed ninety-nine persons, so he began asking whether there was any repentance for him. He came to a monk and asked him, and he said: 'There is no repentance for you.' So he killed the monk. Then he began asking, and then he departed from one village to a village in which there were righteous people. When he was partway along the journey, death overtook him, so he leaned forward with his chest, then died. Thereupon, the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. He was closer to the righteous village by a handspan, so he was counted among its people."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—narrated to us: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Siddiq, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Among those who were before you, there was a man who killed ninety-nine persons. Then he asked about the most knowledgeable of the inhabitants of the earth, and he was directed to a monk. He came to him and said that he had killed ninety-nine persons, so was there any repentance for him? He said: 'No.' So he killed him, completing one hundred with him. Then he asked about the most knowledgeable of the inhabitants of the earth, and he was directed to a scholar. He said that he had killed one hundred persons, so was there any repentance for him? He said: 'Yes, and who can stand between him and repentance? Go to such and such a land, for in it are people who worship Allah, so worship Allah with them, and do not return to your land, for it is an evil land.' So he set out until, when he reached the halfway point of the road, death came to him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. The angels of mercy said: 'He came repentant, turning with his heart to Allah.' And the angels of punishment said: 'He never did any good at all.' Then an angel came to them in the form of a human being, so they appointed him [as an arbitrator] between them. He said: 'Measure the distance between the two lands; whichever of the two he is closer to, he belongs to it.' So they measured it and found him closer to the land that he intended, so the angels of mercy took his soul." Qatadah said: Al-Hasan said: It was mentioned to us that when death came to him, he leaned forward with his chest.

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami and Zuhayr ibn Harb—and the wording is Zuhayr's—narrated to us: 'Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Shaddad narrated to us: Abu Umamah narrated to us, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was in the mosque and we were sitting with him, a man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed an offense incurring a prescribed penalty (hadd), so execute it upon me." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) remained silent toward him. Then he repeated, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed an offense incurring a prescribed penalty, so execute it upon me." He remained silent toward him, and the prayer was established. When the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) finished [the prayer], Abu Umamah said: The man followed the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) when he left, and I followed the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to see what he would reply to the man. The man caught up with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed an offense incurring a prescribed penalty, so execute it upon me." Abu Umamah said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "Did you not, when you left your house, perform ablution and do it well?" He said: "Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Then you attended the prayer with us?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "Then indeed Allah has forgiven you your prescribed penalty"—or he said—"your sin."

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani narrated to us: 'Amr ibn 'Asim narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas, who said: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed an offense incurring a prescribed penalty, so execute it upon me." He said: And the prayer arrived, so he prayed with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). When he concluded the prayer, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed an offense incurring a prescribed penalty, so execute the Book of Allah upon me." He said: "Did you attend the prayer with us?" He said: "Yes." He said: "You have been forgiven."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu al-Nu'man al-Hakam ibn 'Abdullah al-'Ijli narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Ibrahim narrating from his maternal uncle al-Aswad, from 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with the meaning of the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas, and he said in his hadith: Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this specifically for this man, or for us in general?" He said: "Rather, for you in general."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah—and the wording is Yahya's—narrated to us; Yahya said: Abu al-Ahwas informed us, and the other two said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah and al-Aswad, from 'Abdullah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I approached a woman intimately at the furthest edge of Medina, and I took from her what fell short of having intercourse with her. Here I am, so pass whatever judgment you wish concerning me." 'Umar said to him: "Allah had concealed your fault if only you had concealed yourself." He said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did not reply anything, so the man stood up and walked away. Then the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent a man after him who called him back, and he recited this verse to him: {And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember}. A man from among the people asked: "O Prophet of Allah, is this specifically for him?" He said: "Rather, for all people."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, with this chain of transmission, saying: A man took from a woman something short of immoral conduct (intercourse), so he came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who regarded it as grave upon him. Then he came to Abu Bakr, who regarded it as grave upon him. Then he came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Yazid and al-Mu'tamir.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father: Abu 'Uthman narrated to us, from Ibn Mas'ud, that a man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and mentioned that he had taken from a woman either a kiss, or a touch with the hand, or something [similar], as though he were asking about its expiation. He said: So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed [the verse]. Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Yazid.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn al-Jahdari both narrated to us from Yazid ibn Zuray'—and the wording is Abu Kamil's: Yazid narrated to us: Al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that a man took a kiss from a woman, so he came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and mentioned that to him. He said: Thereupon was revealed: {And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember}. He said: The man asked: "Is this for me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "For whoever acts upon it from my ummah."

And Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from Hisham, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from 'Urwah, from Asma', from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "There is nothing possessing more protective jealousy (ghayrah) than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

Yahya said: And Abu Salamah narrated to me that 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to him that Asma' bint Abi Bakr narrated to him that she heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "There is nothing possessing more protective jealousy than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard al-'Ala' with this chain of transmission.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The believer possesses protective jealousy, and Allah is even more jealous."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Aban ibn Yazid and Harb ibn Shaddad narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to the narration of Hajjaj, the hadith of Abu Hurayrah specifically, and he did not mention the hadith of Asma'.

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Hajjaj ibn Abi 'Uthman, who said: Yahya said: And Abu Salamah narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah possesses protective jealousy, and indeed, the believer possesses protective jealousy; and the protective jealousy of Allah is that a believer should commit what He has forbidden to him."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Ishaq said: Jarir informed us, and the other two said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no one to whom praise is more beloved than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; for that reason He praised Himself. And there is no one possessing more protective jealousy than Allah; for that reason He forbade immoralities. And there is no one to whom excuse is more beloved than Allah; for that reason He sent down the Book and dispatched the messengers."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Aba Wa'il saying: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud saying: I asked him: Did you hear it from 'Abdullah? He said: Yes, and he traced it back [to the Prophet], that he said: "There is no one possessing more protective jealousy than Allah; and for that reason He forbade immoralities, both the apparent of them and the concealed. And there is no one to whom praise is more beloved than Allah; and for that reason He praised Himself."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is his: 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no one possessing more protective jealousy than Allah; and for that reason He forbade immoralities, both the apparent of them and the concealed. And there is no one to whom praise is more beloved than Allah."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Ishaq said: Jarir informed us, and 'Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no one to whom praise is more beloved than Allah; for that reason He praised Himself. And there is no one possessing more protective jealousy than Allah; for that reason He forbade immoralities."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Aba 'Ubaydah narrating from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, stretches out His Hand by night so that the sinner of the day may repent, and He stretches out His Hand by day so that the sinner of the night may repent, until the sun rises from its setting place." And Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us with this chain of transmission similar to it.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me: Abu al-Walid narrated to me: Hammam narrated to us: Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah narrated to us, who said: There was a storyteller in Medina called 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amrah; he said: I heard him saying: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "A servant committed a sin..." with the meaning of the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah. And he mentioned three times: "he committed a sin," and in the third: "I have forgiven My servant, so let him do whatever he wills."
Abu Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Zanjawayh al-Qurashi al-Qushayri narrated to me: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad al-Narsi narrated to us with this chain of transmission.

'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad narrated to me: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), regarding what he related from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, who said: "A servant committed a sin and said: 'O Allah, forgive me my sin.' So He, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'My servant committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord Who forgives sin and takes to account for sin.' Then he returned and committed a sin, saying: 'O my Lord, forgive me my sin.' So He, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'My servant committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord Who forgives sin and takes to account for sin.' Then he returned and committed a sin, saying: 'O my Lord, forgive me my sin.' So He, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'My servant committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord Who forgives sin and takes to account for sin; do whatever you will, for I have forgiven you.'" 'Abd al-A'la said: I do not know whether he said in the third or fourth time: "Do whatever you will."

And Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated it to us: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: My father said to me: Qatadah narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us: Shayban ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu al-Walid narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, both from Qatadah; they all mentioned with the chain of transmission of Shu'bah similar to his hadith. And in the hadith of Shayban and Abu 'Awanah: "that a man among the people was granted by Allah abundant wealth and children." And in the hadith of al-Taymi: "for he had not stored up with Allah any good." He said: Qatadah explained it: "he had not preserved with Allah any good." And in the hadith of Shayban: "for, by Allah, he had not stored up (ibta'ara) with Allah any good." And in the hadith of Abu 'Awanah: "had not stored up (imta'ara)" with the letter mim.
